column3: It repeats the faith-and-righteous-work condition and assures that the effort is neither denied nor left unrecorded.

It closely repeats the condition and explicitly assures garden entry without even the smallest injustice.
It supplies the same-Day setting of limited intercession and accepted speech surrounding the focus.

It directly joins belief with freedom from fear of loss or oppressive burden.
It links faith and righteous deeds to divinely granted affection, a distinct favorable outcome.

Musa and Aaron's fear of Pharaoh belongs to a different narrative concern.

It pairs faith and righteous action with the finest recompense and an easeful command.

It contrasts the wrongdoers' fear of earned consequence with believers doing righteous deeds in gardens.

It states that no soul is wronged at all and that each is repaid only for what it used to do.
